purpose: Normative Python behaviors requiring independent Rust implementation, not object-by-object Python interface cloning.

classification.explanation: All Python modules are explicitly classified. Core denotes security-observable behavior, not byte-identical function signatures. Non-core entry points and conformance runners consume core contracts; they do not impose exact Rust CLI, subprocess or fixture parity. New modules require explicit classification.

core_contracts.label: Canonical JSON, request framing, fixed denial/error codes
core_contracts.acceptance: Bidirectional positive/negative canonical wire corpus, status codes and bounds
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Independent Rust development runner now replays all six pure-value corpora and adversarial stream/type cases against Python. This is finite adapter conformance, not native broker integration or all-input CORE-01 parity; freshness proof scope is unchanged. Differential testing also exposed Serde private-marker object coercion; the native decoder now preserves objects explicitly, with guest/provider process regressions. Concrete parser refinement remains open. The native bridge and guest client share extracted bounded newline admission, with real Python/native TLS/Unix cases for clean EOF, coalesced trailing bytes, partial reads and exact limits. Post-send malformed replies are outcome_unknown; this finite framing correspondence does not close JSON/TLS/native mediation or all-input core parity.

core_contracts.label: Binding, epochs, registration, signature and expiry decisions
core_contracts.acceptance: Fresh and stale identity vector cases, exact key and subject binding

core_contracts.label: CA issuance, certificate renewal and current peer pinning
core_contracts.acceptance: Without restarting broker/bridge accept renewed cert/JWT, reject prior epoch on both
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Native same-key renew plus explicit rebind carries the identical broker capability into a current certificate/JWT without restarting account or manifest brokers. Explicit Python/Rust guest bundle installation adds one versioned local certificate/JWT pointer with expected-current digest, held private directories and cooperating reader/writer locks. Both clients consume one snapshot; finite cross-backend live renewal tests cover account and manifest brokers. Host renewal plus guest delivery is not failure-atomic, private-key rotation and rollback protection are not implemented, and broad workflow parity and concrete adapter refinement remain open.

core_contracts.label: Surrogate authentication, delegation, scope and session budgets
core_contracts.acceptance: Matching authorization, denial, delegation and budget transitions (not convenience CLI)
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Opt-in native exact-write approval now uses a separate owner-only host control socket. Actual issue/consume functions are extracted, with a finite 90-row corpus re-evaluated against Python admission and real native provider failure/concurrency/revocation tests. Only the root grant exists; delegation, budgets, broad host CLI/audit compatibility and full CORE-04 parity remain open.

core_contracts.label: Manifest route, operation and disclosure contracts
core_contracts.acceptance: Identical permitted destination/effect and released subset, denied fields and invalid manifests

core_contracts.label: OAuth vault, rotation, refresh ambiguity and epoch fencing
core_contracts.acceptance: Refreshing an access token changes subsequent egress credentials without restarting, stale epochs refused

core_contracts.label: Durable global revocation across authenticated hosts
core_contracts.acceptance: Registered members stop admitting requests after committed tombstone; offline authority fails closed; restart persistent
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Optional native mTLS/SQLite authority and existing Python authority are exercised by independent native/Python broker workflows, frozen exact-response/durable-row vectors, restart/role/concurrency/denial cases. Extracted core peer/operator, terminal tombstone and spent-key decision/history proofs are separate from SQL/TLS/native I/O correspondence. Broad core/all-input parity, independent review and storage/rollback/deployment assumptions remain open. Native host operator activate/revoke/status now uses the existing mTLS protocol without a Python or SQLite client dependency. Both clients require typed receipts and preserve possible committed mutations as outcome_unknown after submission; a missing principal is not a terminal revocation receipt. Pure native receipt validation and its composition with successful extracted revocation are Lean-checked; JSON/TLS/remote-commit correspondence remains separate.

core_contracts.label: Keyed writes: reserve before send and never replay after uncertainty
core_contracts.acceptance: Same principal+key across hosts and restarts at most one provider dispatch; different effect cannot reuse key
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Optional native mTLS/SQLite authority and existing Python authority are exercised by independent native/Python broker workflows, frozen exact-response/durable-row vectors, restart/role/concurrency/denial cases. Extracted core peer/operator, terminal tombstone and spent-key decision/history proofs are separate from SQL/TLS/native I/O correspondence. Broad core/all-input parity, independent review and storage/rollback/deployment assumptions remain open. Native invoke submits named operations and keyed writes through the same protocol; both identity input modes and both coordinator backends are exercised. Host/client share an extracted exact ASCII retry-name validator with a Lean contract; CLI parsing and I/O remain tested adapters.

core_contracts.label: Wire idempotency-key syntax and provider forwarding
core_contracts.acceptance: Coordinated write key required, reserved-derived header on declared operations, no caller header injection
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Native account/manifest coordinator client and keyed manifest writes tested against Python and optional Rust mTLS/SQLite authorities. No all-input parity claim; native request fingerprints now use parsed-policy normalization, compared with Python on finite corpora and real coordinator records; all-input normalization equivalence remains unproved. Native invoke submits named operations and keyed writes through the same protocol; both identity input modes and both coordinator backends are exercised. Host/client share an extracted exact ASCII retry-name validator with a Lean contract; CLI parsing and I/O remain tested adapters.

core_contracts.label: Audit ordering, write ambiguity and guest-visible response confinement
core_contracts.acceptance: No completion before accepted effect; failed provider/transport gives outcome_unknown for writes
core_contracts.implementation_notes: The native bridge and guest client share extracted bounded newline admission, with real Python/native TLS/Unix cases for clean EOF, coalesced trailing bytes, partial reads and exact limits. Post-send malformed replies are outcome_unknown; this finite framing correspondence does not close JSON/TLS/native mediation or all-input core parity. The actual recursive native decoded-key/string reflection guard is now extracted and checked, with exact depth admission and accepted-tree literal exclusion. Finite Python broker/native and provider tests include JSON escapes, nested selected strings and ignored discarded credentials. Serializer/JSON conversion, call-site mediation, alternate encodings and general semantic non-disclosure remain unproved; the final serialized-byte check remains independent.

core_contracts.label: Fail-closed trusted paths, TLS peer pinning, no proxy or redirect
core_contracts.acceptance: Real TLS negative cases, symlink and untrusted root refusal, no bypass of provider network policy

core_contracts.label: HTTPS proxy profiles: strict HTTP/1.1 subset, origin pinning, credential injection and reflection refusal (credential-substitution); exact named-operation translation checked by the host encoder (constrained-http)
core_contracts.acceptance: HP-1 adversarial corpus (smuggling forms, origin/port, session auth, deny list, reflection encodings, revocation inside an open tunnel, oversize, unreachable); HP-4 byte-equality oracle against this reference before any Rust parity claim
core_contracts.implementation_notes: Python reference only (OUT-6, HP-1, HP-2). Substitution makes no authority-confinement claim; constrained-http holds no credential and dispatches through the in-process Broker. See docs/planning/aivm-secrets-http-proxy-profiles.md. Request side extracted in Rust (proxy_http.rs) with byte parity over tests/secrets_vectors/proxy-http-v1.tsv and a proved encoder; response side, native server and constrained-http are Python only.

rust_parity_states.implemented-subset: Rust code is present for a reviewed subset; do not claim complete parity without a runnable differential gate.
rust_parity_states.partial: Rust includes related code but does not implement or validate the entire Python behavior.
rust_parity_states.missing: Rust has no matching implementation for this newly required contract.

parity_rule: Every core contract requires equivalent accepted effects, denials, failure codes and observable traces. Exact class/CLI/OS paths and Rust internal data structures need not match.
non_core_examples: python -m aivm_secrets identity command spelling and help text
gh alias and subprocess adapter UI
AIVM provisioning integration and visual/operator dashboards
Python-only conformance runners, developer scripts, diagnostics and fixtures
Built-in provider presets, local session-directory layout and socket filenames
Operator credential-source aliases and environment-variable resolver strings
Serialization fixture generation and Python package import ergonomics
unverified_boundaries: Single trusted SQLite coordinator host; physical hosts have not been deployed and tested.
No anti-rollback for restoring coordinator storage from an older backup.
Revocation prevents checks after commit, not provider effects already authorized in flight.
Provider Idempotency-Key semantics are provider-specific and not inferred from the header.
Only registered coordinator-aware processes participate; mixed-mode/bypassing hosts are excluded.
Python behavior is tested, not formally proved; Rust proof compilation does not prove Python.
